title: System Design: Scalable URL Shortener (TinyURL / Bitly)

evaluationCriteria: Deep understanding of HTTP Redirection (301 vs 302)
Resilient error handling, monitoring, and legal compliance

functionalRequirements: Shortening: Convert any long URL into a unique, compact short URL.
Redirection: Forward visitors from the short URL to the original long URL with minimal latency.
Custom Short Links (Vanity URLs): Allow users to define custom aliases (e.g., tiny.url/my-portfolio).
Expiration: Support an optional or default expiration date (e.g., 1 year of inactivity).
Analytics: Track engagement metrics (total clicks, referrers, device types, geolocations).
User Accounts: Enable user authentication to manage, edit, and delete their shortened links.
nonFunctionalRequirements: High Availability: 99.99% uptime. The redirection service must remain accessible even if write servers lag.
Ultra-Low Latency: Real-time redirection with sub-10ms cache hits and sub-50ms database hits.
Strict Uniqueness: No two distinct long URLs may receive the same short alias unless explicitly intended.
Non-Predictable: Short URLs should be random and non-sequential to prevent scrapers from enumerating private URLs.
Scalability: Read-heavy system handling thousands of read requests per second smoothly.

assumptions.averageURLSize: 90 bytes (Average Long URL size) + ~410 bytes metadata = ~500 bytes per record

storageEstimations.dailyStorage: 80 Million * 90 bytes = 7.2 GB/day (Raw URL) -> ~40 GB/day with indexes and metadata

memoryAndCaching.paretoPrinciple: 80-20 Rule: 20% of hot URLs generate 80% of read traffic.
memoryAndCaching.verdict: A standard multi-node Redis cluster with 64 GB to 128 GB memory easily holds all hot links in RAM using an LRU eviction policy.

base62Encoding.definition: A 62-character alphanumeric set consisting of [0-9] (10 digits), [a-z] (26 lowercase), and [A-Z] (26 uppercase).
base62Encoding.whyNotBase64: Base-64 introduces reserved URL characters like '+' and '/' which require percent-encoding (%2B, %2F) in query parameters.

lengthCapacityMath.length7: 62^7 = ~3.52 Trillion unique URLs (Easily exceeds our 146 Billion requirement for 5+ years)

md5Approach.howItWorks: Hash the long URL using MD5 (128-bit hex digest) and take the first 6-7 characters.
md5Approach.fatalFlaw: Hash Collisions! Different long URLs can yield identical 7-character prefixes. Resolving collisions requires database lookups, salting, and rehashing in loops, introducing unpredictable latency.

counterBasedBase62Approach.howItWorks: Generate a globally unique 64-bit integer ID first, then convert that integer directly into Base-62.
counterBasedBase62Approach.advantage: 100% collision-free. Every unique integer maps to a unique Base-62 string with zero database collision retries.

zookeeperRangeAllocation.purpose: Coordinates distributed unique integer range allocations across application servers without single points of failure.
howItWorks: ZooKeeper maintains a global atomic counter in its ephemeral znode structure.
When App Server 1 boots up, it requests a range from ZooKeeper. ZooKeeper assigns [1,000,000 to 2,000,000].
When App Server 2 boots up, ZooKeeper assigns [2,000,001 to 3,000,000].
Each application server increments its local atomic counter in memory without making network calls.
When an app server exhausts its range, it queries ZooKeeper for the next unused range chunk (e.g., [3,000,001 to 4,000,000]).
zookeeperRangeAllocation.faultTolerance: If an app server crashes, only its remaining unallocated local range numbers are skipped, which is totally acceptable in a 3.5-trillion-capacity namespace.

http301_PermanentRedirect.behavior: Browsers cache the redirection locally. Subsequent clicks go straight from browser cache to destination.
http301_PermanentRedirect.tradeOff: Saves server load, BUT completely bypasses backend servers, making analytics and click tracking impossible.

http302_TemporaryRedirect.behavior: Browsers always contact the URL shortener service on every click before redirecting.
http302_TemporaryRedirect.tradeOff: Slightly higher server traffic, BUT enables 100% accurate click analytics, bot inspection, and instant link revocation.
http302_TemporaryRedirect.verdict: Use HTTP 302 Found (or 307 Temporary Redirect) for tracking and monetization platforms.

step4_dataModelAndDatabaseDesign.databaseChoice: NoSQL Distributed Key-Value / Wide-Column Store (Cassandra, DynamoDB, or MongoDB)
justification: Access patterns are simple Key-Value lookups (no relational multi-table JOINs required).
Massive horizontal scaling across shards with multi-master replication.
Partition Key is `short_url_text`, providing O(1) single-partition lookups at multi-terabyte scale.

components: Clients: Mobile apps and Web browsers.
DNS / Anycast CDN: Terminates SSL and routes traffic to the nearest regional Point of Presence.
Load Balancer: Nginx / AWS ALB using Consistent Hashing to distribute load to healthy App Servers.
Application Servers: Stateless Flask / Go / Java services executing Base-62 conversions and redirect logic.
ZooKeeper Cluster: Manages distributed numeric ID sequence ranges.
Redis Cache: In-memory LRU cache storing the top 20% most active URLs.
Persistent Database: NoSQL cluster (Cassandra / DynamoDB) storing mapping data.
Async Analytics Pipeline: Kafka message queue + Spark/Flink consumers flushing metrics to ClickHouse / Snowflake.
writeFlow: 1. User sends POST /shorten request with the long URL (and optional custom alias / expiry).
2. Load balancer forwards request to an available application server.
3. If a custom alias is provided, the server verifies whether the alias is available and not a reserved keyword (e.g., 'admin', 'login').
4. If no custom alias is provided, the server fetches the next local sequential integer from its allocated ZooKeeper range.
5. The integer is encoded into a 7-character Base-62 short code.
6. The mapping is persisted to the database and pre-warmed in Redis cache.
7. The short URL is returned to the user.
readFlow: 2. Request hits the Load Balancer and is assigned to an App Server.
3. App Server checks Redis Cache: On Cache Hit -> immediately sends HTTP 302 redirect with Location header.
4. On Cache Miss -> Server queries Database. If found, sets key in Redis with LRU policy and sends HTTP 302 redirect.
5. If link is expired or does not exist, returns HTTP 404.
6. Concurrently, an asynchronous telemetry event is emitted to Apache Kafka for analytics processing without slowing down user redirect.

linkExpirationHandling.problem: Running periodic batch scripts like `DELETE FROM urls WHERE expires_at < NOW()` locks tables and triggers heavy disk IOPS.
linkExpirationHandling.solution: Combine two patterns: (1) Lazy / Passive Expiration on read (if current timestamp > expiry timestamp, return 404 and evict from cache); (2) Native Database TTL policies (Redis EXPIRE and DynamoDB TTL daemons clean up cold dead records in the background without affecting app servers).

securityAndAbusePrevention.rateLimiting: Enforce Token Bucket or Sliding Window rate limiting per IP / API token at the API Gateway level (e.g., 50 req/min for free users) to prevent automated link-generation spam.
securityAndAbusePrevention.malwareAndPhishingDefense: Integrate Google Safe Browsing API or a Bloom filter blacklist on the write path to intercept known malicious domains before generating short aliases.

loggingMonitoringAndAlerting.telemetry: Export P99 read/write latency, Cache Hit Ratio, and 4xx/5xx HTTP error rate metrics into Prometheus and visualize via Grafana.
loggingMonitoringAndAlerting.alerting: Trigger automated PagerDuty / SMTP alerts if Redis cache hit ratio drops below 70% or 5xx server errors exceed 1% over a 5-minute rolling window.

systemDesignProblem: Design Agoda / Hotel & Accommodation Booking Platform

overview.coreChallenge: Massive search volume with complex filtering (location, dates, prices, amenities), avoiding double-booking during high concurrent traffic, low-latency room inventory management, and multi-currency/multi-language localization.

importantFeatures.detail: Search properties by location, check-in/check-out dates, guest count, price ranges, star ratings, and amenities.
Customer authentication, saved favorites, booking history, and personalized recommendation feeds.
Real-time room availability validation, temporary inventory locking, payment gateway processing, and booking confirmation.
Verified customer reviews, ratings submission, and weighted aggregate review scores.
Dynamic currency conversion via real-time FX rates and multilingual listing translations.

storageEstimation.mediaStorageStrategy: Photos/Videos stored in Amazon S3 / Google Cloud Storage backed by Cloudflare / CloudFront CDN edge caching; metadata stored in NoSQL/RDBMS.

trafficThroughputQPS.verdict: Requires distributed in-memory caching (Redis/Memcached) and horizontally scaled Elasticsearch clusters to offload search traffic from persistent databases.

apiDesign.description: Registers a new user account on Agoda.
Retrieves properties based on location, dates, budget, and amenities.
Creates a temporary reservation and locks room inventory for 10 minutes.

response200.message: Booking created. Inventory locked for 10 mins.

doubleBookingPrevention.problem: Two concurrent users attempt to book the last available Deluxe Room for the same check-in dates simultaneously.
solutionTwoPhaseReservation: Phase 1 (Temporary Hold): When user reaches the checkout/payment page, acquire a distributed Redis lock on the room inventory key (`LOCK:hotel_101:room_A:2026-10-10`). Decrement inventory temporarily with a 10-minute TTL.

Phase 2 (Confirmation): Upon payment success from Payment Gateway webhook, execute an atomic SQL update with optimistic locking: `UPDATE room_inventory SET available_count = available_count - 1 WHERE room_type_id = 12 AND date BETWEEN '2026-10-10' AND '2026-10-15' AND available_count > 0`.
Rollback: If payment fails or the 10-minute timer expires, release the temporary Redis lock and increment inventory counter back automatically.

searchEngineArchitecture.mechanism: Elasticsearch indices partitioned by Geo-hashes (QuadTree / S2 Geometry). Properties within latitude/longitude radius are filtered using fast inverted indexes across amenities and price filters in sub-20ms without querying transactional RDBMS.

dynamicCurrencyEngine.mechanism: Base prices are stored in hotel's native currency (e.g. THB for Thailand, JPY for Japan). Real-time FX exchange rates are refreshed into Redis every 15 minutes. The API Gateway transforms prices to the user's localized currency preference at runtime.

systemDesignProblem: Design a Scalable Payment Gateway (Razorpay / Stripe)

overview.definition: Razorpay is a robust, developer-first online payment gateway that enables merchants and businesses to accept, process, and disburse digital payments securely across cards, UPI, Net Banking, and digital wallets.
overview.coreMission: Simplify online transactions, eliminate payment failure points via intelligent routing, ensure zero financial inconsistency, and maintain bank-grade security (PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance).

importantFeatures.detail: Accepts multi-source payments: Credit/Debit Cards (Visa, Mastercard, RuPay), Net Banking (50+ banks), UPI (Google Pay, PhonePe, Paytm), Wallets, and EMI.
Generates dynamic or static shareable URLs sent via SMS, WhatsApp, or Email allowing customers to pay instantly without website checkout integration.
Manages automated recurring payments (UPI Autopay, e-Mandates, Card standing instructions), supporting trials, prorated billing, and automated dunning (retry on failure).
Dynamically directs transactions to optimal payment gateways and bank acquirers based on real-time success rates, network latency, fee structures, and downtime health checks.
Automated matching of merchant orders, gateway transactions, and bank settlement payout files (UTR tracking) to simplify enterprise accounting.
Robust REST APIs, Webhook event notification engines, and mobile/web client SDKs (Checkout.js, React Native, Flutter, iOS, Android).

assumptions.readToWriteRatio: 100:1 (Read-heavy for dashboards, checking order status, analytics)
assumptions.transactionsRecordedPerDay: 4,000,000 / 100 = 40,000 writes/day (simulated baseline; in real production all 4M writes are recorded in an append-only ledger)

storageEstimation.dailyStorage: 40,000 transactions/day * 1 KB = 40 MB/day (Baseline assumption) -> In full 4M transactions/day: 4 GB/day
storageEstimation.threeYearStorage: 40 MB * 365 days * 3 years ≈ 43.8 GB (Baseline) -> Full production with audit logs: ~4.38 TB to 10 TB
storageEstimation.storageStrategy: Relational/CockroachDB with row-level encryption for ACID transactions; cold transactional logs archived to Amazon S3 / HDFS.

trafficThroughputQPS.peakQPS: Peak surge (festive sales / flash deals) typically 10x to 50x of average ≈ 500 to 2,500 transactions/second

scalingPillars.horizontalScalability: Stateless API server clusters auto-scaling based on CPU and request latency metrics behind load balancers.
scalingPillars.cachingMechanism: In-memory Memcached/Redis clusters storing user auth sessions, merchant API keys, payment method metadata, and bank downtime flags.
scalingPillars.distributedLoadBalancing: Layer 7 Load Balancers (AWS ALB, Nginx) distributing TLS 1.3 encrypted client traffic using consistent hashing and round-robin.
scalingPillars.databaseSharding: Partitioning transaction tables horizontally by `merchant_id` or `user_id` to distribute write IOPS across multiple primary nodes.

relationships: Users to Transactions: 1 to Many (One user/merchant executes multiple transactions).
Users to PaymentMethods: 1 to Many (One user can save multiple cards/UPI accounts).
Transactions to Refunds: 1 to Many (A transaction can have one or more partial/full refunds).
Users to Subscriptions: 1 to Many (A customer can subscribe to multiple recurring plans).

components: Mobile / Web Clients: Customers and merchants interacting via Checkout SDKs or merchant apps.
CDN (Cloudflare / CloudFront): Caching static payment forms, logos, and JavaScript SDK bundles (Checkout.js).
Load Balancer: Distributes encrypted HTTPS requests across application servers.
API Gateway: Centralized point for API key authentication, rate limiting (Token Bucket), and TLS termination.
Application Servers: Business logic workers executing payment orchestrations.
Cache (Redis / Memcached): Low-latency cache for token validation and smart-routing health tables.
Database (PostgreSQL / CockroachDB): Strong ACID compliance for ledger entries and transactions.
Distributed Storage (Amazon S3 / HDFS): Archiving daily settlement files, invoices, and transaction raw logs.

twoPhasePaymentFlow.phase1_Authorize: Customer enters card/UPI details -> Gateway contacts Issuing Bank via Acquirer -> Bank locks/holds funds -> Returns AUTHORIZED state.
twoPhasePaymentFlow.phase2_Capture: Merchant confirms order fulfillment -> Gateway commits the charge -> Returns CAPTURED state. If order fails, hold expires or sends VOID.

idempotencyAndDuplicatePrevention.theProblem: Customer double clicks 'Pay Now' or network drops cause the merchant's server to retry payment creation, risking charging the customer twice.
idempotencyAndDuplicatePrevention.theSolution: Client sends unique `Idempotency-Key` (UUIDv4) in HTTP header. The gateway saves `SET lock:idempotency:<key> PENDING NX EX 120`. If an identical request arrives while processing or completed, the cached response is returned immediately without re-initiating bank debits.

pciDssComplianceAndTokenization.cardVault: Raw card numbers (PAN) are NEVER stored in regular application databases. Card numbers are passed into an isolated, audited Card Vault. The vault encrypts the PAN with AES-256 and returns an opaque Token (`tok_9a8f2b`) used by downstream services.

webhookReliabilityWithExponentialBackoff.mechanism: When payment captures, Webhook service pushes event to Kafka (`payment.captured`). Worker posts payload with HMAC-SHA256 signature to merchant's server. If merchant server responds with 5xx or times out, retry queue schedules delivery with exponential backoff + jitter: 10s, 30s, 2m, 15m, 1h, 6h.

parameters: Historical success rate over past 10 minutes
Payment method type (HDFC Netbanking routed to direct HDFC integration)

systemDesignProblem: Design a Scalable Music Streaming Service (Apple Music / Spotify)

overview.definition: Apple Music is a premier global subscription-based audio streaming service that allows users to stream and download tens of millions of songs, albums, and curated playlists seamlessly across devices.
overview.coreChallenge: Handling ultra-low latency audio streaming without playback buffering, distributing multi-petabyte audio catalogs globally via edge CDNs, managing DRM (Digital Rights Management) for copyright protection, and serving personalized machine learning recommendations at scale.

importantFeatures.detail: On-demand streaming access to millions of songs, albums, artist pages, and curated playlists.
Dynamic recommendation feeds (e.g. Discovery Station, New Music Daily) based on collaborative filtering, user listening history, and audio embeddings.
Continuous live streaming radio (Apple Music 1) and algorithmic infinite radio stations generated from a seed song or artist.
Downloading encrypted audio chunks for offline listening with FairPlay / Widevine DRM license expiration checks.
Follow artists/friends, share playlists, like songs, and post community comments.

assumptions.songsPerUserPerDay: 5 songs listened per user per day
assumptions.dailyNewSongsUploaded: (1 / 100) * 500 Million = 5 Million songs/day (or catalog ingestion batches)

storageEstimation.storageStrategy: Audio files are encoded into multiple bitrates (AAC, ALAC Lossless) and stored in S3/Ceph object storage across distributed availability zones.

trafficThroughputQPS.networkBandwidth: 5,787 streams/sec * 5 MB ≈ 28.9 GB/sec (Continuous egress offloaded to global Edge CDNs)

scalingPillars.horizontalScaling: Stateless microservice pods deployed across multi-region Kubernetes clusters.
scalingPillars.caching: Multi-tier caching: Edge CDN (audio bytes), Redis clusters (user sessions, playlists, hot metadata).
scalingPillars.cdnDelivery: Edge Points of Presence (Cloudflare, Akamai, Fastly) terminate 95%+ of audio chunk requests.
scalingPillars.databaseSharding: Horizontally partitioned Cassandra / DynamoDB clusters sharded by `user_id` and `song_id`.

relationships: Users to Playlists: 1 to Many
Albums to Songs: 1 to Many
Playlists to Songs: Many to Many (via PlaylistSongs join table)
Users to Songs (Likes/Comments): Many to Many

components: Client Applications: Native iOS, macOS, Android, and Web clients running audio player engines.
Global CDN Edge: Caching audio chunks (.m4s, .ts) and HLS manifests close to users for sub-200ms playback initiation.
Layer 7 Load Balancer: Routing requests to healthy API Gateway instances.
API Gateway: Centralized authentication, rate limiting, and request routing.
Distributed Cache (Redis): Storing user playlists, listening state, and hot catalog metadata.
Metadata Database (Cassandra / DynamoDB / PostgreSQL): Storing relational models and social interactions.
Blob Storage (Amazon S3): Storing master lossless audio assets and trans-coded multi-bitrate chunks.

microservices.name: Audio Ingestion & Transcoding Service
microservices.responsibility: Receives lossless FLAC/ALAC masters from record labels, transcodes them into multi-bitrate AAC/ALAC streams, generates HLS/DASH byte chunks, and encrypts payloads with DRM keys.

microservices.name: Catalog & Search Service
microservices.responsibility: Indexes songs, albums, and artist metadata inside Elasticsearch for sub-second autocomplete and faceted search.

microservices.name: Streaming & License Service
microservices.responsibility: Authenticates user active subscription and delivers short-lived DRM decryption keys (Apple FairPlay).

microservices.name: Playlist & User Interaction Service
microservices.responsibility: Handles playlist creation, collaborative additions, song liking, and user social comments.

microservices.name: Personalization & Recommendation Engine
microservices.responsibility: Processes listening history streams via Apache Kafka + Apache Spark to compute matrix factorizations and vector similarity embeddings (ANN / Milvus).

audioStreamingArchitecture.protocol: HLS (HTTP Live Streaming) / MPEG-DASH over HTTP/2 & HTTP/3.
audioStreamingArchitecture.chunkingMechanism: Songs are sliced into small 4-second to 6-second audio segments (.m4s). A master playlist (`.m3u8` manifest) indexes the segment URLs.
audioStreamingArchitecture.adaptiveBitrateStreaming: If the user is on 5G, the client player downloads 256kbps or Lossless chunks. If network drops to 3G, the client automatically steps down to 64kbps chunks mid-playback without stalling audio.
audioStreamingArchitecture.preloadingStrategy: The client app aggressively prefetches the first 2 chunks (8 seconds) of the next queued track in the playlist to achieve instantaneous 0ms track skipping.

drmAndOfflineEncryption.mechanism: Audio chunks stored on CDNs and user device disks are AES-128 encrypted. When the user plays a song, the client requests a DRM license from the License Server. The server verifies the Apple Music subscription and delivers the session decryption key inside a hardware-isolated secure enclave.

realTimeRecommendationPipeline.flow: Listening events (SongPlay, Skip, Like) -> Ingested into Apache Kafka (`user-listen-events`) -> Processed by Apache Flink for real-time radio tuning -> Stored in Feature Store -> Vector embedding similarity queries run against Pinecone/Milvus to return similar tracks in milliseconds.

systemDesignProblem: Design a Scalable Live Cricket Streaming Platform (CricHD / Hotstar)

overview.definition: CricHD is a high-concurrency live sports streaming and cricket community platform that provides real-time match streaming, video highlights, ball-by-ball commentary, player statistics, interactive fan chats, and personalized feeds across mobile, desktop, and smart TVs.
overview.coreChallenge: Serving ultra-low latency live video feeds (under 3-5 seconds broadcast delay) to tens of millions of concurrent viewers during high-traffic peak matches (e.g. India vs Pakistan, IPL finals), managing live score state updates with sub-second accuracy, and scaling community chat threads without crashing servers.

importantFeatures.detail: Adaptive Bitrate (ABR) live video streaming using Low-Latency HLS (LL-HLS) and MPEG-DASH across multiple resolutions (1080p, 720p, 480p, 360p).
On-demand short video clips, key wickets, boundaries, and condensed post-match highlight packages.
Historical batting/bowling averages, head-to-head records, strike rates, and live in-game player metric trackers.
Live ball-by-ball text commentary, expert analysis, and automated scorecard updates delivered via push channels.
Live match chat rooms, interactive fan prediction polls, social sharing, and user likes/comments on video highlights.
Machine-learning driven video discovery based on user viewing history, followed teams, and favorite players.

storageEstimation.storageStrategy: Master video recordings and compressed ABR chunks stored in AWS S3 / Google Cloud Storage multi-region buckets; hot segments cached on Edge CDNs.

trafficThroughputQPS.networkBandwidthEgress: 10 Million concurrent users streaming at 2 Mbps avg = 20 Tbps (Offloaded 98%+ to multi-CDN tier: Akamai, Fastly, Cloudflare)

liveVideoStreamingPipeline.ingestion: High-bitrate RTMP / SRT camera feed sent from cricket ground production control room to Ingestion Gateway.
liveVideoStreamingPipeline.transcoding: Hardware GPU encoders convert master video into 4 ABR profiles: 1080p (4.5 Mbps), 720p (2.5 Mbps), 480p (1.2 Mbps), 360p (600 Kbps).
liveVideoStreamingPipeline.packaging: Packs chunks into Low-Latency HLS (LL-HLS) with 1-second segment lengths (.m4s) and delta playlist updates (`.m3u8`), reducing live latency from 30s to 3s.
liveVideoStreamingPipeline.cdnOriginShielding: An Origin Shield layer sits between global CDNs and transcoding servers so edge nodes fetch newly formed chunks from the shield rather than overloading the origin transcoders.

ballByBallRealtimeDelivery.architecture: Scorer enters ball outcome -> Hits Score Gateway -> Updates Redis cache -> Redis Pub/Sub publishes to `match:123:score` -> WebSocket gateway pushes event to connected viewer devices instantly without polling.

liveChatAtScale.theProblem: 10 million fans chatting in the same match room creates 100,000 messages/second, overwhelming client DOMs and WebSocket pipes.
liveChatAtScale.theSolution: Dynamic Chat Sharding & Sampling: Divide fans into virtual chat rooms of 500 users each, or rate limit message ingestion to display a sampled stream of 20 high-quality messages/second per client.

systemDesignProblem: Design a Scalable E-Commerce Ecosystem (Alibaba / Taobao / Tmall)

flashSaleInventoryArchitecture.theProblem: During flash sales (Singles' Day), 100,000 users click 'Buy Now' on an item with only 500 units in stock within 1 second. Traditional SQL row-locking (`SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`) exhausts connection pools and deadlocks the database.
theSolutionMultiTierInventory: 1. Traffic Shaping / Rate Limiting: Sentinel gateway throttles bot bursts and passes only realistic checkout volumes.

2. Redis / Tair In-Memory Reservation: Inventory is pre-warmed into Redis. Atomic stock deduction runs via a Lua script (`EVAL` script checks `if stock >= qty then redis.call('decrby', key, qty) return 1 else return 0`).

3. Asynchronous Database Settlement: If the Lua script succeeds, an event is pushed to RocketMQ/Kafka (`OrderCreated`). Background workers batch-insert order rows into PolarDB asynchronously without blocking the user response.
4. Auto-Rollback: If the user fails to complete Alipay payment within 15 minutes, a delayed message triggers an automatic inventory increment back into Redis and marks the order as CANCELLED.

databaseShardingStrategy.dualKeyIndexing: Orders are sharded by `user_id` so that customers can query their entire order history in a single shard lookup. For merchants who need to query all orders for their store, an asynchronous Change Data Capture (CDC via Canal) replicates order records into a secondary Elasticsearch/HBase store sharded by `seller_id`.

crossBorderLatencyOptimization.unitArchitecture: Data is partitioned into self-contained units (Cells). Users in Southeast Asia are mapped to Singapore data centers where reads are answered locally, with asynchronous bi-directional replication syncing back to the primary Hangzhou data center.

emailBroadcastPipeline.theProblem: When an author with 200,000 subscribers clicks 'Publish', sending 200,000 emails synchronously inside the web request will timeout and crash the server.
theSolutionAsynchronousFanout: 1. Author hits 'Publish' -> Post status changes to PUBLISHED in PostgreSQL.
2. An event `PostPublished(post_id, author_id)` is published to Apache Kafka.
3. An Email Coordinator service queries active subscribers for that author in cursor-based batches of 1,000.
4. Coordinator pushes 200 chunk tasks into a Celery/RabbitMQ job queue.

5. A distributed pool of 50 background worker containers pull chunk tasks, compile personalized HTML (including reader-specific 1-click unsubscribe links and tracking pixels), and dispatch via AWS SES / SendGrid connection pools.
6. Bounce and delivery webhooks stream back to the Analytics Service to update open/bounce rates.

hybridFanoutModel: Fanout-on-Write (Push): For authors with under 50,000 subscribers, publishing a post pushes the `post_id` directly into the Redis sorted set (`feed:user_id`) of every active subscriber.

Fanout-on-Read (Pull): For celebrity authors with millions of subscribers, posts are not pushed to all followers. Instead, when a reader opens Substack, the Feed Service pulls the latest posts from those mega-authors and merges them with the user's cached timeline on the fly (SLA < 350ms).

paywallEnforcement.mechanism: When an unauthenticated or free user requests a paid post, the API server truncates the `content` payload at the teaser boundary on the server side before returning JSON to the browser. The full body is never sent to the client to prevent inspect-element bypasses.

systemDesignProblem: Design a Scalable Instant Messenger (WhatsApp / Telegram / Slack)

overview.definition: An Instant Messenger (IM) is a high-concurrency, low-latency real-time communication platform enabling users to exchange 1-on-1 and group text messages, multimedia attachments, presence statuses, and read receipts across mobile, desktop, and web clients.
overview.coreChallenge: Maintaining tens of millions of persistent bi-directional WebSocket / TCP connections simultaneously, ensuring sub-100ms message delivery latency globally, managing real-time user presence (online/offline heartbeat tracking), guaranteeing strictly ordered message delivery without duplicates, and enforcing End-to-End Encryption (E2EE).

importantFeatures.detail: Instant bidirectional text messaging over persistent duplex connections with offline queueing.
Three-state message delivery lifecycle: Sent (single check), Delivered (double check), Read (blue double check).
Tracks whether contacts are online, offline, or typing, powered by ephemeral heartbeat ping/pong mechanisms.
Contact synchronization, phone address book discovery, and blocklist management.
Sharing images, videos, audio notes, and files via chunked uploads to object storage with CDN-accelerated previews.
Triggering APNs / FCM alerts when recipient devices are disconnected from active WebSocket sessions.
Double Ratchet Algorithm (Signal Protocol) ensuring messages cannot be decrypted by intermediate servers or telecom carriers.
Local SQLite database search on mobile devices, complemented by encrypted server-side synchronization.

connectionManagementAndMessageDeliveryFl.step1_Connection: Client opens WebSocket connection to WebSocket Gateway. Gateway writes `user_id -> gateway_instance_id` to Redis Session Store.
connectionManagementAndMessageDeliveryFl.step2_Sending: User A sends message to User B. Gateway A accepts message, generates a monotonic distributed Snowflake ID, writes to Cassandra, and publishes event to Kafka.
connectionManagementAndMessageDeliveryFl.step3_Routing: Message Router checks Redis for User B's gateway location.
connectionManagementAndMessageDeliveryFl.caseOnline: If User B is connected to Gateway B, Router forwards packet to Gateway B via internal gRPC; Gateway B pushes packet down User B's socket.
connectionManagementAndMessageDeliveryFl.caseOffline: If User B is offline (no Redis session key), packet is sent to Push Notification Service (FCM/APNs). When User B reconnects, client sends last synced `message_id`, and Gateway queries Cassandra for missed messages.

groupChatFanoutStrategy.smallGroups: Fanout-on-Write: For groups under 500 members, the message is duplicated into each member's private message mailbox, optimizing read latency.
groupChatFanoutStrategy.largeChannels: Fanout-on-Read: For broadcast channels (up to 100,000 members), a single message is written to the group timeline. Members pull new messages using a cursor when their chat window is actively open.

presenceEngineHeartbeat.mechanism: Every client sends a lightweight ping every 30 seconds. Gateway refreshes Redis key with a 60-second TTL. If client drops Wi-Fi or closes app, key expires naturally without requiring an explicit disconnect signal. Friends subscribed to this user get presence updates via Redis Pub/Sub.

endToEndEncryptionSignalProtocol.mechanism: The chat server acts only as an encrypted envelope router. Public identity keys and One-Time Prekeys are published to the Key Service. User A computes a shared secret locally using X3DH (Extended Triple Diffie-Hellman) and encrypts text using Double Ratchet. The server cannot inspect or modify plaintext.

Upvoting and downvoting on posts and comments with strict 1-vote-per-user enforcement and vote retraction.
Arbitrarily deep nested reply trees allowing contextual discussions with collapsible subtrees.
Time-decay scoring balancing vote velocity and publication age to keep the front page fresh and dynamic.
Live score counters, dead post flags, automated anti-spam filters, and shadowbanning for abusive actors.

parameters: P: Upvotes of the post (subtracting 1 to discount submitter's initial vote).
T: Time elapsed since submission in hours (T = (current_time - submission_time) / 3600). Adding 2 prevents division by zero and tempers newly created posts.
G: Gravity factor (default G = 1.8 on Hacker News). Higher gravity accelerates score decay, pulling older stories off the front page.
hackerNewsRankingAlgorithm.cachingStrategy: Do NOT calculate this formula on every HTTP request! A background cron worker iterates active posts submitted within the last 48 hours every 60 seconds, calculates Score, and updates a Redis Sorted Set (`ZADD frontpage:ranked <score> <post_id>`). The read API simply executes `ZREVRANGE frontpage:ranked 0 29` in sub-millisecond O(log N) time.

hierarchicalCommentTreeArchitecture.theProblem: Recursive relational parent-child lookups (`parent_id`) cause N+1 query loops and heavy database overhead when fetching 1,000 comments for a single post.
theSolutionMaterializedPath: Store a string path for each comment: e.g. root comment has path '0001', a reply to it has '0001.0001', a nested reply has '0001.0001.0001'.
Fetching all comments of a post requires a single SQL query: `SELECT * FROM comments WHERE post_id = ? ORDER BY path ASC`.
The client or API gateway converts the linearly ordered list into a nested JSON tree in O(N) linear time without database recursions.

mechanisms: Rate Limiting: Max 30 votes per minute per IP address.
Vote Ring Detection: Graph analysis flagging clusters of accounts that repeatedly upvote the same author's links within minutes.
Shadowbanning: Banned or flagged spam accounts can still submit links and comments, but their posts are invisible to other users (`dead = true`), preventing spammers from adapting.

systemDesignProblem: Design Facebook Timeline Function (User Profile & Activity History)

overview.definition: Facebook Timeline is a personalized, reverse-chronological profile feature that organizes and showcases a user's life events, status posts, uploaded photos, videos, and social interactions over time. overview.coreChallenge: Timeline differs fundamentally from the dynamic News Feed: while News Feed aggregates updates from hundreds of friends using machine learning ranking, Timeline represents an individual user's complete historical archive requiring sub-50ms reverse-chronological retrieval across years of posts, strict privacy access control enforcement per viewer, and efficient cursor-based pagination across millions of historical items.

importantFeatures.detail: Displays all user activities, status updates, and shared content ordered strictly from newest to oldest with deep historical jumping (by year/month).
Supports rich media formats including text status, single/album high-res photos, videos, and shared link previews.
Special milestone events (Graduation, New Job, Marriage, Relocation) pinned with customized iconography and distinct layout formatting.
Per-post access control lists (Public, Friends Only, Friends Except, Only Me, Custom Lists) evaluated dynamically based on viewer identity.
Private management dashboard where the profile owner can review, untag, hide, or permanently delete past posts and interactions.
Allows the user to pin important posts to the top of the timeline irrespective of their original chronological publication date.

scalingPillars.loadBalancing: Layer 7 Load Balancers routing requests using consistent hashing on `target_user_id` to maximize cache locality.
scalingPillars.databaseSharding: Sharding database instances by `user_id` so that an individual's entire timeline data resides on a single database partition/shard.

Users to Posts: 1 to Many (A user authors multiple posts on their timeline).
Users to LifeEvents: 1 to Many (A user records multiple milestone events).

Users to Users (Friends/Follows): Many to Many (Bi-directional friendship or directional follow graph).

chunkingAndDeltaSyncPipeline.chunkSize: Fixed 4 MB chunks (or Content-Defined Chunking using Rabin Fingerprints / FastCDC to prevent whole-chunk offset shifting upon single-byte insertions).
uploadWorkflow: 1. Client modifies a 100MB file (e.g., appends text at the end).
2. Client chunks file into 25 blocks of 4MB and computes SHA-256 for each chunk.
3. Client queries Metadata Server: `POST /chunks/check_hashes` sending the list of 25 hashes.
4. Server checks Redis/Cassandra: 24 chunks already exist in storage; only 1 chunk is new.
5. Client transmits ONLY the 1 modified 4MB chunk to the Block Server (saving 96% bandwidth).
6. Client commits the new version manifest (list of 25 hashes in order) to the Metadata Server.
7. Metadata Server commits the transaction and notifies the Notification Service.

globalDeduplicationEngine.mechanism: Before any chunk is uploaded, its cryptographic hash (`chunk_hash`) is looked up globally. If User A uploads an identical 4MB video chunk that User B already uploaded, User A's file version simply links to the existing S3 key, incrementing `reference_count`. Zero additional cloud storage is consumed.

conflictResolutionStrategy.theProblem: User edits a file on Laptop A while offline on a flight, while simultaneously editing the same file on Desktop B at home.
theSolutionBranchingFork: 1. Desktop B commits Version 2 first to the server.
2. Laptop A comes online and attempts to commit Version 2 with a different chunk hash list.
3. Metadata Server rejects Laptop A's commit with HTTP 409 Conflict because its base version is stale.
4. Laptop A pulls Version 2, preserves its local changes, and automatically saves a duplicate file named: `Document (Alice's conflicted copy 2026-10-02).docx`.
5. The user inspects both files and merges changes manually without silent data overwrites.

longPollingVsWebsocketsForSync.decision: WebSockets are preferred for active bi-directional communication on desktop/mobile sync clients. When clients operate behind restrictive corporate firewalls or proxies blocking persistent TCP sockets, the system gracefully falls back to Long-Polling (holding an HTTP GET request open for up to 60 seconds until a new chunk notification occurs).

import dropbox
from dropbox.paper import PaperDocCreateUpdatePolicy
import os

# Demonstrating official SDK methods
TOKEN = 'YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN'
dbx = dropbox.Dropbox(TOKEN)

def upload_file(local_path, remote_path):
    with open(local_path, "rb") as f:
        dbx.files_upload(f.read(), remote_path)

def download_file(remote_path, local_path):
    _, res = dbx.files_download(remote_path)
    with open(local_path, "wb") as f:
        f.write(res.content)

def sync_folder(local_folder, remote_folder):
    if not os.path.exists(local_folder):
        os.makedirs(local_folder)
    result = dbx.files_list_folder(remote_folder)
    for entry in result.entries:
        local_file_path = os.path.join(local_folder, entry.name)
        if not os.path.exists(local_file_path) or entry.server_modified > os.path.getmtime(local_file_path):
            _, res = dbx.files_download(entry.path_lower)
            with open(local_file_path, "wb") as f:
                f.write(res.content)

def create_paper_doc(title, content):
    paper_api = dropbox.paper.PaperApi(dbx)
    doc = paper_api.docs_create(title, import_format="markdown")
    paper_api.docs_update(doc.doc_id, revision=PaperDocCreateUpdatePolicy.overwrite.any(), contents=content)
    return doc.doc_id

def share_public_link(file_path):
    link = dbx.sharing_create_shared_link_with_settings(file_path).url

geospatialIndexingAndDriverMatching.spatialPartitioning: DoorDash divides geographical maps into hexagonal cells using Uber H3 (Resolution 7 or 8, ~1km edge length). Restaurants and Dashers are indexed by their current H3 cell.
dispatchAlgorithmBipartiteMatching: 1. Order is marked `ACCEPTED_BY_REST` by the merchant tablet.
2. The Dispatch Engine searches the restaurant's H3 cell and neighboring 6 concentric rings for available Dashers in Redis (`GEORADIUS`).
3. A cost matrix is computed evaluating: (Distance to restaurant) + (Predicted kitchen prep time remaining) + (Dasher acceptance rating).
4. The order offer is sent to the highest-ranked Dasher with a 30-second acceptance countdown.
5. If rejected or timed out, the offer cascades immediately to the next candidate Dasher.

dynamicEtaPredictionEngine.formula: Total ETA = Estimated Prep Time (T_prep) + Dasher Travel to Restaurant (T_pickup) + Dasher Travel to Customer (T_dropoff).
dynamicEtaPredictionEngine.machineLearningRefinement: Historical meal prep models predict cooking duration based on kitchen load and item complexity (e.g. 10 pizzas take longer than 1 salad). If the kitchen is running behind, Dasher dispatch is intentionally delayed so couriers don't wait idle in restaurants.

gpsTelemetryOptimization.theProblem: 100,000 couriers pinging GPS every 3 seconds generates 33,000 writes/second. Writing every raw coordinate synchronously to PostgreSQL degrades database performance.
theSolutionWriteBehindCaching: 1. Dasher app sends `{ driver_id, lat, lng, order_id }` via lightweight UDP / gRPC / WebSocket to the Telemetry Gateway.
2. Gateway updates Redis in-memory store (`GEOADD active_dashers lat lng driver_id`) in sub-milliseconds.
3. Redis publishes to a WebSocket channel (`order:12345:track`) which streams directly to the waiting customer's map screen.
4. Telemetry coordinates are pushed into an Apache Kafka topic in batches. Background workers flush downsampled points to cold storage for billing audits.

orderLifecycleStateMachine.transitions: SUBMITTED -> ACCEPTED_BY_REST -> PREPARING -> READY_FOR_PICKUP -> PICKED_UP / OUT_FOR_DELIVERY -> DELIVERED (or CANCELLED). Each transition is verified against allowable next states to prevent out-of-order race conditions.

doubleEntryBookkeepingLedger.corePrinciple: Every monetary transaction must have balanced debits and credits: `Sum(Debits) == Sum(Credits)`. Account balances are computed directly from the append-only ledger entries rather than a single mutable balance column.

idempotencyAndTwoPhaseLocking.theProblem: Client taps 'Pay $500', network drops before receipt arrives; client retries. Without protection, $1,000 is deducted.
theSolutionIdempotencyKeyWithRedis: 1. Client generates UUIDv4 `Idempotency-Key` and attaches it to the HTTP header.
2. API Gateway checks Redis: `SET lock:idempotency:<key> PENDING NX EX 120`.
3. If key exists with status PENDING, the incoming duplicate is rejected with HTTP 409 Conflict.
4. If key exists with status COMPLETED, the gateway returns the cached transaction response without re-processing.
5. If key is new, the server acquires locks on the sender's account in sorted order, executes the transfer, saves the receipt to the idempotency store, and returns HTTP 200.

distributedSagaPatternForBankRails.mechanism: Bank transfers take 1-3 business days. The transfer service uses an Orchestrated SAGA pattern: (1) Reserve funds in PayPal wallet (State: PENDING); (2) Dispatch ACH Debit task to bank integration worker; (3) If ACH succeeds, commit ledger entry (State: SETTLED); (4) If ACH fails (insufficient funds), execute compensating transaction to release wallet hold (State: FAILED).

realTimeFraudDetectionPipeline.flow: Transaction event emitted -> Kafka topic `payments.eval` -> Flink stream worker calculates velocity features (e.g. 5 transactions in 60 seconds from new IP) -> Machine Learning model scores transaction from 0 to 1000 -> If Score > 800: Block immediately; If 500-800: Challenge with SMS OTP / 2FA; If < 500: Allow.

hotstarHighConcurrencyLiveStreamingArchi.theProblem: When Virat Kohli hits a boundary during a World Cup final, 50 million concurrent users request the next 2-second video segment within 100 milliseconds. If requests reach origin servers, the entire infrastructure collapses (Thundering Herd Problem).
theSolutionMultiTierOriginShielding: 1. Live Camera Ingestion: Stadium OB-vans send uncompressed SRT/RTMP video feeds to redundant AWS MediaLive / GPU transcoding clusters.
2. Chunking & Packaging: Video is split into 2-second CMAF (Common Media Application Format) segments packaged with Low-Latency HLS (LL-HLS) manifests.
3. Origin Shielding: Transcoders push chunks to an intermediate Origin Shield caching layer (Varnish / Nginx cache cluster).
4. Multi-CDN Edge Caching: Global CDNs (Akamai, Cloudflare, Fastly) fetch new segments ONCE from the origin shield and cache them at thousands of edge Points of Presence (PoPs).
5. 99.8% CDN Cache Hit Ratio: 49.9 million requests are terminated directly at edge PoPs within 5-15ms, with zero origin load.

concurrentDevicePlaybackLimiter.mechanism: Every active client sends a lightweight heartbeat ping every 30 seconds (`POST /playback/heartbeat` with `user_id` and `device_id`). The service updates a Redis Hash: `HSET sessions:<user_id> <device_id> <timestamp>` with a 60-second TTL. If `HLEN sessions:<user_id>` exceeds the plan limit (e.g., 2 devices for VIP, 4 for Premium), the oldest playback lease is revoked, and the client displays 'Too many active screens'.

dynamicAdaptiveBitrateStreaming.algorithm: Client video players monitor chunk download speed and device buffer levels continuously. If the buffer falls below 4 seconds or network throughput drops, the player immediately steps down to a lower bitrate (e.g. 1080p -> 720p -> 480p) without stalling the video stream.

feedGenerationLRUCaching.mechanism: Personalized user feeds are pre-computed by background Spark/Flink workers using user watch history and collaborative filtering. The top 50 personalized feed items are cached in Memcached using an LRU eviction strategy. When a user opens the app, the feed loads in under 50ms.

audioStreamingAndChunkDelivery.transcodingProfiles: Uploaded tracks are transcoded into Ogg Vorbis (Desktop/Android) and AAC (iOS/Web) at 96kbps (Low), 160kbps (Standard), and 320kbps (High Quality).
chunkingAndPrefetching: 1. Audio files are partitioned into sequential encrypted chunks.
2. When a track starts, the client requests Chunk 0 immediately.
3. While playing Chunk 0, the client player aggressively prefetches Chunks 1 and 2.
4. The client also pre-caches the first 500 KB of the NEXT track in the playlist queue to achieve 0ms gapless playback upon song transition.
audioStreamingAndChunkDelivery.localClientCache: Desktop and mobile clients allocate up to 10 GB of local storage to cache played tracks (encrypted with local AES-128 keys). Replaying a song draws 100% from local disk, saving cellular bandwidth and CDN egress costs.

recommendationEngineDiscoverWeekly.matrixFactorizationALS: Decomposes the User-Item interaction matrix into low-dimensional latent vector spaces (128-dimensional embeddings).
recommendationEngineDiscoverWeekly.vectorSearchWithAnnoy: Spotify's open-source Annoy (Approximate Nearest Neighbors Oh Yeah) library builds tree-based indices to query nearest neighbor tracks in sub-millisecond times.

spotifyConnectArchitecture.mechanism: A centralized Playback State Router keeps an active WebSocket pipe to every connected device owned by the user. wechatSyncProtocol.concept: Instead of pushing individual messages blindly to clients, WeChat uses a pull-driven Sync Protocol inspired by Microsoft ActiveSync.
howItWorks: 1. Every user has a strictly monotonic 64-bit sequence counter in the database: `sync_key`.
2. When User A sends a message to User B, the server assigns a new sequence number (e.g. `seq = 105`) and saves it to User B's mailbox.
3. The server sends a lightweight 4-byte 'SyncNotify' packet over User B's LongLink TCP connection.
4. User B's client responds with a `SyncRequest(local_sync_key = 104)`.
5. The server returns all messages where `seq > 104` (in this case, message 105) and updates the client's `local_sync_key` to 105.
6. If the connection drops, upon reconnecting the client simply sends its last known `sync_key` and receives all missed messages seamlessly without duplicates.

momentsMutualFriendPrivacyAlgorithm.thePrivacyRule: If Alice posts a Moment, and Bob comments on it, Charlie can ONLY see Bob's comment if Charlie is friends with BOTH Alice AND Bob. Strangers cannot see each other's interactions even on the same post.
implementation: 2. The service queries the Friend Graph (Redis Set): `friends:Charlie`.
3. For each comment on the post written by User X, the server checks: `if X == Charlie or X in friends:Charlie then show else hide`.
4. This is evaluated dynamically on the read path in O(1) time using Redis `SISMEMBER`.

miniProgramSandboxArchitecture.dualThreadModel: To prevent rogue JavaScript code from freezing the UI or accessing unauthorized memory, WeChat separates execution into two isolated threads:
miniProgramSandboxArchitecture.viewThread: Runs in a standard WebView, responsible strictly for DOM rendering, WXML templates, and WXSS styling.
miniProgramSandboxArchitecture.logicThread: Runs inside a headless JavaScriptCore / V8 virtual machine with no direct DOM access. All native hardware access (Camera, GPS, Bluetooth) is bridged via asynchronous JSON message passing through WeChat native runtime.

wechatPayRedPacketConcurrency.theProblem: A celebrity sends a Red Packet of 10,000 RMB split among 50,000 users. 1 million users click 'Open' within 2 seconds. A single SQL row update (`UPDATE wallet SET balance = ...`) would deadlock the database.
theSolutionPreAllocationAndMemoryQueuing: 1. Split-on-Creation: When the sender creates the Red Packet, all 50,000 amounts are pre-calculated (using Double-Average Random algorithm) and pushed into a Redis List (`LPUSH packet:123:money 5.20 12.50 ...`).
2. Grabbing: When a user clicks 'Open', the server executes atomic `RPOP packet:123:money`. If a value is popped, the user wins that amount immediately in memory.

3. Async Settlement: The winning claims are pushed to RocketMQ/Kafka. Background ledger workers asynchronously debit the sender's escrow and credit winners' wallets in bulk batches without database contention.

from flask import Flask, request, jsonify
from datetime import datetime
import uuid

app = Flask(__name__)

users_db = {}
messages_db = []
moments_db = []
friendships_db = {} # user_id -> set of friend_ids
sync_keys_db = {}   # user_id -> current monotonic sequence int

class User:
    def __init__(self, u_id, username, password, email=None):
        self.user_id = u_id
        self.username = username
        self.password = password
        self.email = email

@app.route('/api/users', methods=['POST'])
def register_user():
    data = request.get_json() or {}
    username = data.get('username')
    password = data.get('password')
    if not username or not password:
        return jsonify({'error': 'Invalid username or password.'}), 400
    
    u_id = 'usr_' + str(uuid.uuid4())[:8]
    user = User(u_id, username, password, data.get('email'))
    users_db[u_id] = user
    friendships_db[u_id] = set()
    sync_keys_db[u_id] = 0
    return jsonify({'message': 'User registration successful.', 'user_id': u_id}), 201

@app.route('/api/messages', methods=['POST'])
def send_message():
    data = request.get_json() or {}
    sender_id = data.get('sender_id')
    receiver_id = data.get('receiver_id')
    content = data.get('content')

    if not sender_id or not receiver_id:
        return jsonify({'error': 'Invalid sender or receiver ID.'}), 400

    # Increment receiver's monotonic sequence key for WeChat Sync Protocol
    sync_keys_db[receiver_id] = sync_keys_db.get(receiver_id, 0) + 1
    seq_id = sync_keys_db[receiver_id]

    msg_id = 'msg_' + str(uuid.uuid4())[:8]
    msg_record = {
        'message_id': msg_id,
        'sender_id': sender_id,
        'receiver_id': receiver_id,
        'content': content,
        'sequence_id': seq_id,
        'timestamp': datetime.utcnow().isoformat()
    }
    messages_db.append(msg_record)
    return jsonify({'message': 'Message sent successfully.', 'message_id': msg_id, 'sequence_id': seq_id}), 200

@app.route('/api/sync', methods=['POST'])
def sync_messages():
    data = request.get_json() or {}
    user_id = data.get('user_id')
    client_sync_key = data.get('sync_key', 0)

    # Pull delta messages where sequence_id > client_sync_key
    deltas = [m for m in messages_db if m['receiver_id'] == user_id and m['sequence_id'] > client_sync_key]
    current_server_key = sync_keys_db.get(user_id, 0)

    return jsonify({'new_sync_key': current_server_key, 'messages': deltas}), 200

@app.route('/api/moments', methods=['POST'])
def post_moment():
    data = request.get_json() or {}
    user_id = data.get('user_id')
    content = data.get('content')
    if not user_id:
        return jsonify({'error': 'Invalid user ID.'}), 400

    mmt_id = 'mmt_' + str(uuid.uuid4())[:8]
    moment = {
        'moment_id': mmt_id,
        'user_id': user_id,
        'caption': content,
        'image_url': data.get('image_url'),
        'timestamp': datetime.utcnow().isoformat(),
        'comments': []
    }
    moments_db.append(moment)
    return jsonify({'message': 'Moment posted successfully.', 'moment_id': mmt_id}), 201

if __name__ == '__main__':
    app.run(port=5000, debug=True)

feedFanoutHybridArchitecture.problem: Pure Fanout-on-Write (Push) breaks when a celebrity with 50M followers posts (writing to 50M mailboxes causes massive write spikes). Pure Fanout-on-Read (Pull) causes high read latency when an active user follows 2,000 accounts.
hybridSolution: 1. Standard Users (< 50,000 followers): Use Fanout-on-Write (Push). When they post, a background task pushes the post ID into each follower's Redis Sorted Set (`timeline:<user_id>`).
2. Celebrities / High-Follower Accounts (> 50,000 followers): Use Fanout-on-Read (Pull). Their posts are NOT pushed to follower inboxes. Instead, they are stored in the author's own timeline.

3. Timeline Merge on Read: When a user requests their home feed, the Feed Service reads their cached Redis timeline and dynamically pulls & merges the latest posts from any celebrity accounts they follow, returning the sorted top 30 posts in sub-50ms.

trendingTopicsRealtimePipeline.mechanism: User post submissions and search queries emit events into Apache Kafka (`topic_events`). An Apache Flink streaming job consumes the events and maintains a sliding window (e.g., past 1 hour) using a Count-Min Sketch algorithm to compute frequency bursts: `Score = (Frequency_Current_Hour - Base_Frequency) / (Age_Hours + 2)^1.5`. The top 50 topics are refreshed into a Redis Sorted Set every 10 seconds.

celebrityHotspotCacheStampedeMitigation.mechanism: When a major celebrity breaks news, millions of users query the exact same post simultaneously. To prevent cache breakdown (Thundering Herd): (1) Mutex / Distributed Lock: Only one worker queries the database on a cache miss while others wait; (2) Cache Warm-up & Early Expiry: Background cron workers proactively refresh hot post caches before TTL expires.

import psycopg2

class WeiboDatabaseRepository:
    def __init__(self, host, dbname, user, password):
        self.conn = psycopg2.connect(host=host, database=dbname, user=user, password=password)
        self.cur = self.conn.cursor()

    def create_post(self, user_id, content):
        query = "INSERT INTO posts (user_id, content, timestamp) VALUES (%s, %s, NOW()) RETURNING post_id"
        self.cur.execute(query, (user_id, content))
        post_id = self.cur.fetchone()[0]
        self.conn.commit()
        return post_id

    def get_feed(self, user_id, limit=30):
        query = """
            SELECT p.post_id, p.user_id, p.content, p.timestamp 
            FROM posts p
            INNER JOIN follows f ON p.user_id = f.following_id
            WHERE f.follower_id = %s
            ORDER BY p.timestamp DESC
            LIMIT %s
        """
        self.cur.execute(query, (user_id, limit))
        return self.cur.fetchall()

    def add_follow(self, follower_id, following_id):
        query = "INSERT INTO follows (follower_id, following_id, timestamp) VALUES (%s, %s, NOW()) ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING"
        self.cur.execute(query, (follower_id, following_id))
        self.conn.commit()

directToS3PresignedUploadPipeline.theProblem: If 1,000 photographers upload 25MB RAW files simultaneously through the API gateway, web servers suffer severe bandwidth exhaustion, thread starvation, and timeouts.
theSolutionDirectPresignedUploads: 1. Client requests upload ticket: `POST /api/images/presign` sending file size, MIME type, and checksum.
2. API Server authenticates user, verifies daily upload quotas, and returns an Amazon S3 Presigned URL.
3. Client uploads the raw image directly to S3 via HTTP PUT (bypassing backend servers entirely).

geospatialIndexingQuadTreeVsH3.quadtreeLimitations: QuadTrees partition 2D space into 4 equal quadrants recursively. When population density shifts, nodes split dynamically. However, QuadTrees struggle with dynamic updates (moving drivers constantly force tree re-balancing locks) and distorted boundary distances.
uberH3HexagonalArchitecture: 1. Hexagonal Geometry: Uber uses H3, a discrete global grid system based on hexagons. Unlike squares, hexagons have an identical distance from the center to all 6 adjacent neighbors, eliminating directional bias in radius queries.
2. Resolution Hierarchy: Resolution 7/8 (~0.5km to ~1km area) is used for city dispatch. Each hexagon has a unique 64-bit integer ID (`h3_index`).

3. Real-Time Indexing in Redis: Moving drivers update their position in Redis via `HSET h3:<hex_id> <driver_id> '<lat>,<lng>'`. Finding nearby drivers is a simple O(1) set union across the target hex and its 6 immediate ring neighbors (`kRing(hex, 1)`).

mechanism: 1. Rider requests a ride at coordinate (P_lat, P_lng).
2. System identifies the Rider's H3 cell and pulls available drivers from that cell and adjacent concentric rings.
3. Route Engine computes ETA for each candidate driver using real-time traffic road networks.

4. Batch Matching: Instead of greedily assigning the single closest driver immediately, DISCO batches requests over 3-5 second windows to maximize global supply efficiency and minimize cumulative wait times across all riders.
5. The match offer is dispatched to the chosen driver with a 15-second acceptance timer. If rejected or timed out, the offer cascades to the next best driver.

dynamicSurgePricingEngine.mechanism: Every 15-30 seconds, a stream worker aggregates riders opening the app in H3 cell `H` (demand) and unassigned available drivers in `H` (supply). If demand significantly outpaces supply, the surge multiplier increases in increments (e.g. 1.2x, 1.5x, 2.0x). This incentivizes nearby drivers to reposition toward high-surge zones while moderating rider demand.

driverLocationBroadcastPipeline.flow: Driver App pings GPS every 4s -> WebSocket Gateway -> Updates Redis in-memory cache -> Publishes to Kafka `driver-locations` -> Location Broadcast Service streams position to riders with open app views in that H3 cell (4:1 subscription ratio) via WebSockets without querying the persistent database.

import asyncio
import json
import websockets

# In-memory mapping: channel_id -> set of active websocket connections
channel_subscriptions = {}
# Connection to user mapping
connected_users = {}

async def handler(websocket):
    user_id = None
    subscribed_channels = set()
    try:
        async for raw_message in websocket:
            data = json.loads(raw_message)
            event_type = data.get('type')

            # Client handshake & authentication
            if event_type == 'AUTH':
                user_id = data.get('user_id')
                connected_users[user_id] = websocket
                await websocket.send(json.dumps({'status': 'CONNECTED', 'user_id': user_id}))

            # Subscribe to channel stream
            elif event_type == 'SUBSCRIBE_CHANNEL':
                channel_id = data.get('channel_id')
                if channel_id not in channel_subscriptions:
                    channel_subscriptions[channel_id] = set()
                channel_subscriptions[channel_id].add(websocket)
                subscribed_channels.add(channel_id)
                await websocket.send(json.dumps({'status': 'SUBSCRIBED', 'channel_id': channel_id}))

            # Send message and broadcast to all members in that channel
            elif event_type == 'SEND_MESSAGE':
                channel_id = data.get('channel_id')
                content = data.get('content')
                broadcast_payload = json.dumps({
                    'event': 'NEW_MESSAGE',
                    'channel_id': channel_id,
                    'sender_id': user_id,
                    'content': content,
                    'timestamp': asyncio.get_event_loop().time()
                })
                
                # Fan-out broadcast to all open sockets in this channel
                if channel_id in channel_subscriptions:
                    subscribers = list(channel_subscriptions[channel_id])
                    await asyncio.gather(*[sub.send(broadcast_payload) for sub in subscribers if sub != websocket])

    except websockets.exceptions.ConnectionClosed:
        pass
    finally:
        # Clean up subscriptions on disconnect
        for ch in subscribed_channels:
            if ch in channel_subscriptions and websocket in channel_subscriptions[ch]:
                channel_subscriptions[ch].remove(websocket)
        if user_id in connected_users:
            del connected_users[user_id]

async def main():
    server = await websockets.serve(handler, '0.0.0.0', 8765)
    await server.wait_closed()

if __name__ == '__main__':
    asyncio.run(main())

resumableUploadFlow: 1. Client calls `POST /api/v1/videos/upload-session` to initiate upload with total file size and MD5/SHA256 checksum.
2. Upload Service returns unique Upload ID and S3 pre-signed chunk URLs (using TUS protocol for pause/resume).
3. Client streams 5 MB - 10 MB chunks. If mobile connection drops at 70%, client queries server for last confirmed byte offset and resumes seamlessly.
4. Once all chunks land in S3 Staging Bucket, S3 fires an `ObjectCreated` event to Kafka topic `video.uploaded`.
distributedTranscodingDAG: 1. Transcoding Orchestrator consumes `video.uploaded` event and determines optimal encoding profiles (e.g., 4K AV1, 1080p H.264, 720p, 480p).
2. Chunk Splitter splits large video into 10-second GOP (Group of Pictures) chunks and schedules tasks across GPU/CPU worker pods.
3. FFmpeg processes chunks in parallel, joins them, and generates HLS playlist `.m3u8` and media segments `.ts`.
4. Master playlist and media files upload to Production S3 Bucket, thumbnail generator extracts keyframes, and DB status updates to `READY`.

adaptiveBitrateStreamingAndABR.mechanism: Player pehle master manifest (`master.m3u8`) download karta hai jisme sabhi bitrates (360p @ 600kbps, 720p @ 2500kbps, 1080p @ 5000kbps) listed hote hain. Player live bandwidth measure karta hai: agar user ka WiFi slow hota hai, player seamless tarike se lower-resolution segment request karta hai bina video buffer ya freeze hue.

privacyAndDomainLockSecurity.domainRestrictionWorkflow:
Jab koi website (e.g. `clientdomain.com`) video embed karti hai:
1. Video player embed iframe load karta hai aur Playback Service ko request bhejta hai.
2. Service incoming HTTP request ke `Referer` aur `Origin` headers check karti hai against video ki `allowed_domains` list.
3. Agar allowed hai, toh Service ek short-lived (15 minutes) HMAC-signed CDN streaming token generate karti hai.
4. CDN edge token verify karke hi `.m3u8` playlist aur media chunks serve karta hai. Direct video link sharing block ho jati hai.

analyticsBufferingAndWriteOptimization.mechanism: 34.7K requests/sec par har video play ko direct database me update karna write bottleneck create karega. Isliye, video player har 10 seconds me lightweight telemetry beacon (`POST /api/v1/telemetry/heartbeat`) bhejta hai. Yeh events Kafka topic `video-views-stream` me jate hain. Apache Flink worker stream aggregate karta hai aur Redis HyperLogLog use karke unique viewers count karta hai. Hourly batch updates hi relational database me persist hoti hain.

acidLedgerAndDoubleSpendingPrevention.problem: Agar ek user ke paas $50 balance hai aur woh simultaneously do $50 ke transactions execute karta hai, toh race condition me account negative ho sakta hai.
solutionArchitecture: 1. Idempotency Key Handling: Client har transaction request ke saath UUID generate karke bhejta hai (`Idempotency-Key: uuid`). API Gateway Redis me check karta hai; agar key already processed hai, toh cached result return karta hai bina dobara charge kiye.

2. Pessimistic Row-Level Locking: Database level par `SELECT balance FROM users WHERE user_id = :sender_id FOR UPDATE` execute hota hai. Sender ka row lock ho jata hai jab tak transaction commit ya rollback na ho.

3. Double-Entry Bookkeeping: Direct `users.balance` modify karne ke bajaye ek immutable `LedgerEntries` table me do rows insert hoti hain (Debit Sender $50, Credit Receiver $50). Sum of debits must strictly equal sum of credits. Trigger balance update atomic transaction ke andar hi rehta hai.

mechanism: 1. Transaction Complete Event: Payment commit hote hi event Kafka topic `payment-completed` par emit hota hai with payload `{tx_id, sender_id, receiver_id, note, privacy: 'FRIENDS'}`.

2. Privacy Filter Worker: Consumer check karta hai:
   - PRIVATE: Event ko feed generation pipeline se turant drop kar deta hai.
   - FRIENDS: Sender aur Receiver ke common friends fetch karta hai aur unki personal timeline queues me push karta hai.
   - PUBLIC: Global public feed Redis sorted set (`ZADD public_feed <timestamp> <tx_id>`) me add karta hai.
3. Read Pipeline: User jab feed kholta hai, toh app pre-computed Redis list se direct instant feed fetch karti hai bina costly SQL joins ke ($O(1)$ lookup).

flow: 1. User A browser creates WebRTC PeerConnection, captures local microphone/camera media stream, and generates SDP Offer.
2. SDP Offer is sent over WebSocket to Signaling Server, which forwards it to User B.
3. User B receives offer, sets RemoteDescription, captures their media, generates SDP Answer, and sends it back.
4. Both browsers exchange ICE candidates (IP address and port tuples obtained from STUN server).
5. Once candidate pair is selected, direct peer-to-peer encrypted UDP media flow begins. If symmetric NAT blocks direct connection, media seamlessly routes through TURN relay.

systemDesignProblem: Design a Planetary-Scale Distributed Web Crawler (Googlebot / Bingbot / Internet Archive)

overview.definition: Web Crawler (spider bot) ek autonomous distributed software system hai jo internet ke billions of web pages ko systematically discover, download, parse aur extract karta hai. Iska primary use case Search Engine Indexing (Google/Bing), Web Archiving (Wayback Machine), Web Mining & Content Monitoring, aur Copyright/Infringement detection hota hai.
overview.coreChallenge: Internet scale par graph cycle loops aur spider traps se bachna, strict Host Politeness guarantee karna (single target web server ko overload na karna via robots.txt遵守), billions of URLs me duplicates ko sub-millisecond me filter karna (Bloom Filter / In-Memory Bitmaps), dynamic JavaScript-heavy single-page applications (SPAs) render karna, asynchronous non-blocking I/O network pipelines scale karna, aur petabytes of HTML content ko distributed storage (S3/HDFS) me compress karke store karna.

importantFeatures.detail: Seed URLs se start karke page links extract karna aur breadth-first search (BFS) traversal ke zariye web graph discover karna.
URLs ko unki page authority (PageRank), freshness, aur importance ke basis par prioritize karna, while enforcing domain-level rate limiting.
Target website ke robots.txt rules parse karke follow karna aur successive requests ke beech predefined cooldown delay (e.g. 500ms - 2s) ensure karna.
Visited URLs ko Bloom Filters ke through filter karna aur duplicate HTML content ko cryptographic hashing (SimHash / MD5) se discard karna.
Client-side rendered React/Angular/Vue web pages ko headless browsers (Puppeteer/Playwright) ke through evaluate karna.
Raw HTML, CSS, aur media assets ko compressed WARC (Web ARChive) format me date-wise versioning ke saath preserve karna.
Plagiarism aur stolen intellectual property detect karne ke liye regular expression pattern matching aur text fingerprinting run karna.
Web pages ki historical change frequency track karke dynamic recrawl interval set karna (news sites daily, static blogs monthly).

urlFrontierArchitecture.problem: Frontier ko simultaneously do mutually exclusive goals balance karne hote hain: High Priority pages ko pehle crawl karna (Importance) aur kisi bhi single web server ko bombard na karna (Politeness).
twoTierQueueDesign: 1. Priority Queues (F-Frontier): Inbound URLs importance score (PageRank, domain trust) ke basis par $K$ priority queues me split hote hain. Prioritizer high-score queues se zyada traffic pop karta hai.
2. Politeness Queues (B-Frontier): URLs domain name ke basis par $B$ separate queues me place hote hain (`hash(domain) % B`).

3. Queue Selector & Delay Heap: Har politeness queue se exactly ek request at a time fetch hoti hai. Request complete hone ke baad domain queue ko Min-Heap delay queue me daal diya jata hai (`ready_timestamp = now + crawl_delay`). Ye structure target website ko DDOS hone se 100% protect karta hai.

pipeline: 1. URL Normalization: Trailing slashes remove karna (`/about/` -> `/about`), lowercase hostname (`HTTP://EX.COM` -> `http://ex.com`), default ports strip karna (`:80`, `:443`), aur tracking query params (`utm_source`, `ref`) discard karna.

2. Bloom Filter Verification: 64-bit integer hash compute karke Redis Bloom Filter me test kiya jata hai (`BF.ADD visited_urls <normalized_url>`). Agar bit array me present hai, toh page download hone se pehle hi drop ho jata hai (Zero network IOPS wasted).

3. Content Fingerprinting: Agar different URLs identical content render karte hain (mirrors), toh SimHash/MinHash Hamming distance compute hota hai. Agar distance <= 3 bits ho, toh document discard kar diya jata hai.

dynamicContentHandling.mechanism: Har URL ke initial lightweight HTTP response ko check kiya jata hai. Agar body empty ho aur script tags heavy hon (SPAs like React), request queue route hoti hai Headless Chrome Cluster (Puppeteer/Playwright) par. Worker pool page ko load karke network idle hone tak wait karta hai (hydration), dynamic DOM snapshot capture karta hai, aur DOM parsing pipeline ko handoff kar deta hai.

countermeasures: 1. Maximum Path Depth Limiter: URL path me 8 slashes se zyada depth hone par auto-drop (e.g., `/calendar/2026/10/02/...`).
2. Repeating Pattern Detection: Regex filter detect karta hai cyclic loop patterns jaise `/dir1/dir2/dir1/dir2`.
3. Size & Timeout Constraints: HTTP response body 10 MB par hard-terminate hoti hai aur socket read timeout 10 seconds par close ho jata hai.

import asyncio
import aiohttp
from bs4 import BeautifulSoup
from urllib.parse import urlparse, urljoin
import time

class AsyncProductionCrawler:
    def __init__(self, concurrency_limit=10, per_host_delay=1.0):
        self.visited_urls = set()
        self.frontier = asyncio.Queue()
        self.concurrency_limit = concurrency_limit
        self.per_host_delay = per_host_delay
        self.last_host_access = {}
        self.lock = asyncio.Lock()

    def normalize_url(self, base_url, link):
        joined = urljoin(base_url, link)
        parsed = urlparse(joined)
        # Strip fragments and trailing slashes for deduplication
        path = parsed.path.rstrip('/') if parsed.path != '/' else '/'
        return f"{parsed.scheme}://{parsed.netloc.lower()}{path}"

    async def can_fetch_host(self, host):
        async with self.lock:
            now = time.time()
            last_time = self.last_host_access.get(host, 0.0)
            if now - last_time < self.per_host_delay:
                return False
            self.last_host_access[host] = now
            return True

    async def fetch_page(self, session, url):
        try:
            headers = {'User-Agent': 'ProductionCrawlerBot/2.0 (+http://example.com/bot)'}
            async with session.get(url, headers=headers, timeout=aiohttp.ClientTimeout(total=8)) as response:
                if response.status == 200 and 'text/html' in response.headers.get('Content-Type', ''):
                    html = await response.text()
                    return html
                return None
        except Exception as e:
            return None

    async def worker(self, worker_id, session):
        while True:
            url = await self.frontier.get()
            host = urlparse(url).netloc

            # Enforce politeness per host
            while not await self.can_fetch_host(host):
                await asyncio.sleep(0.2)

            html = await self.fetch_page(session, url)
            if html:
                soup = BeautifulSoup(html, 'html.parser')
                title = soup.title.string.strip() if soup.title and soup.title.string else 'No Title'
                print(f"[Worker {worker_id}] Crawled: {url} | Title: {title}")

                # Extract links
                for tag in soup.find_all('a', href=True):
                    raw_link = tag['href']
                    clean_link = self.normalize_url(url, raw_link)
                    
                    async with self.lock:
                        if clean_link.startswith('http') and clean_link not in self.visited_urls:
                            self.visited_urls.add(clean_link)
                            await self.frontier.put(clean_link)

            self.frontier.task_done()

    async def run(self, seed_urls):
        for seed in seed_urls:
            norm_seed = self.normalize_url(seed, '')
            self.visited_urls.add(norm_seed)
            await self.frontier.put(norm_seed)

        connector = aiohttp.TCPConnector(limit=100, ttl_dns_cache=300)
        async with aiohttp.ClientSession(connector=connector) as session:
            tasks = [asyncio.create_task(self.worker(i, session)) for i in range(self.concurrency_limit)]
            # Run crawler until initial batch finishes or timeout
            await asyncio.sleep(3)
            for t in tasks: t.cancel()

if __name__ == '__main__':
    crawler = AsyncProductionCrawler(concurrency_limit=5, per_host_delay=1.0)
    seeds = ['https://example.com']
    asyncio.run(crawler.run(seeds))

operationalTransformationOTDeepDive.problem: Do users A aur B simultaneously ek hi document par type karte hain. Document me 'CAT' hai. User A index 0 par 'B' add karta hai ('BCAT'). User B simultaneously index 3 par 'S' add karta hai ('CATS'). Agar bina transformation ke apply karenge toh document corrupt ho jayega.
solutionArchitecture: 1. Operation Definition: Operation consists of operations like `Insert(pos, char)` and `Delete(pos, len)` with base `revision_num`.
2. Server Central Authority: Server har document ke liye strictly sequential revision counter (`rev 0 -> 1 -> 2 ...`) maintain karta hai.

3. Transformation Function `T(op1, op2)`: Jab User B ka operation (`opB`) server par aata hai with base `rev 0`, lekin server already User A ka `opA` (insert at 0) commit karke `rev 1` par ja chuka hai, toh server `opB' = Transform(opB, opA)` execute karta hai. Kyunki index 0 par ek character add ho chuka hai, User B ka insertion index 3 se shift hokar 4 ban jata hai (`Insert(4, 'S')`).

4. Exact Convergence: Transformed operation execute hokar document 'BCATS' ban jata hai, aur server User A aur User B dono ko transformed ACK bhejta hai. Both clients mathematically identical state par pahunch jate hain.

crdtVsOtTradeOff.comparison: Google Docs traditionally uses Operational Transformation (OT) kyunki isme centralized server revision enforce karta hai, jisse metadata payload tiny (few bytes) rehta hai. CRDTs (Conflict-free Replicated Data Types, e.g., Yjs/Automerge) completely decentralized P2P offline systems ke liye best hain, lekin har character ke sath 50-100 bytes ka unique ID metadata carry karna padta hai jo 1.5 PB/day scale par memory footprint explode kar deta hai.

mechanism: 1. Offline Buffering: Disconnect hone par client-side buffer local edits ko save karta rehta hai (`[op1, op2, ...]` against `last_synced_rev`).
2. Reconnect Handshake: Client server ko bhejta hai: 'I have operations from Rev 5'.
3. Server Catch-Up: Server client ko Rev 5 se Rev 20 tak ke sabhi intermediate committed operations stream karta hai.
4. Client-Side Rebase: Client local OT engine intermediate 15 operations ke against apne buffered offline operations ko rebase karta hai.
5. Upstream Push: Rebased operations server ko push hote hain aur bina kisi data loss ke document history me seamlessly merge ho jate hain.

snapshotCompactionPipeline.mechanism: Operation table me billions of rows ho sakti hain. Jab kisi document me 100 operations accumulate ho jate hain, Background Worker complete in-memory text tree ko evaluate karke ek full snapshot (JSON/Protobuf) Google Cloud Storage par write karta hai (`doc_101_rev_500.snap`). Jab koi naya user document open karta hai, toh woh 0 se 500 replay karne ke bajaye seedhe rev 500 snapshot load karta hai aur sirf recent 10 uncommitted operations replay karta hai (Time-to-Open < 150ms).
